page: Amazon Web Services m5.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance deployed on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon Platinum 8259CL processor clocked at 3.1 GHz, providing 4 vCPUs derived from 2 dedicated physical cores across 2 threads per core. The instance includes 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction support covers AVX, AVX-512F, and AES cryptography extensions, backed by 35 MB of L3 cache. It does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, relying instead on network-attached storage, and provides a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results place the processing and memory subsystems predominantly in the lower tier relative to broader cloud hardware. The instance registered a Geekbench single-core score of 1035.0 and a multi-core score of 2250.0, alongside a PassMark CPU rating of 3995.73. Memory subsystem benchmarks show an average PassMark memory score of 1971.82, with large block uncached read speeds of 26.12 GB/sec and write speeds of 22.79 GB/sec. Application testing reflected 3.32 million Redis SET operations per second and a static web serving throughput of 3.89 GB/sec. Language model inference on small 135M parameter models reached 158.5 tokens per second for prompt processing and 60.38 tokens per second for generation.

The primary tradeoff of the m5.xlarge stems from its reliance on previous-generation Intel microarchitecture and lack of built-in NVMe disks. While the balanced resource distribution provides predictable performance for non-bursting workloads, its compute throughput per core lags behind newer architectures. In qualitative terms, the instance serves as a standard budget-predictable general-purpose option for mid-tier enterprise deployments. Workloads well matched to this profile include small-to-midsize relational databases, containerized backend services, standard web serving tiers, and steady-state staging or integration environments.
description: Amazon Web Services m5.xlarge is a Nitro-based general-purpose server powered by a 4-vCPU Intel Xeon Platinum 8259CL x86_64 processor clocked at 3.1 GHz across 2 physical cores. It features 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, adhering to a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM allocation, and provides a baseline network speed of 1 Gbps. The server carries no local storage or GPUs, requiring networked block volumes for disk I/O. Benchmark assessments locate its computational and memory throughput largely in the entry-to-moderate performance bands, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 2250.0 and 3.32 million Redis SET operations per second. Given its balanced resource footprint and dedicated allocation, m5.xlarge is suited for standard enterprise workloads including moderate web serving, container management, CI/CD runners, and mid-tier backend business applications.
